statement: Host launch must use at_npu::native::OpCommand::RunOpApi("Name", [=]() -> int {...}) with value capture; do not call the launch function outside it.
UB -> GM stores must go through a VECOUT queue (TQue<QuePosition::VECOUT,N>); do not store from a VECCALC tensor.
Never read or write GM scalars from the kernel (errcode 264/95); row/stride arithmetic must be scalar per program or host-side, and per-element integer division is very slow.
16bit -> float cast uses CAST_NONE; float -> 16bit cast uses CAST_RINT. Match the golden fp32 accumulation and cast-on-store semantics.
Vector base addresses must be 32B aligned. DataCopyPad with blockCount>1 requires the per-block byte length to be a multiple of 32B; otherwise copy one row at a time.
int8 data cannot use the UB block-copy path; Compare (tensor-tensor) is not verified on this stack.
950PR currently rejects the triton route at staged eval after a successful wheel build; use AscendC/aclnn/direct-launch for 950PR.
The submission must not use torch/torch_npu compute APIs, CPU fallbacks, or non-contiguous outputs; the canonical compute must be in the AscendC kernel.
The zip root must contain build.sh; it runs without arguments and must produce dist/cann_bench*.whl within 600s. Layout follows one of the official scaffolds.
On 950PR, short non-aligned rows are usually faster on the SIMT path; long rows use the tile/DMA path. Do not assume a 910B kernel is correct or fast on 950.
SwiGlu official cases cover dim in {-1,0,1,2}, 1-5D, prime/odd sizes, fp16/fp32/bf16, and +-inf/NaN inputs. Correctness must cover all of them, not just the benchmark shape.
950PR AscendC builds use build.sh --soc=ascend950 (Bisheng dav-3510); 910B uses --soc=ascend910b (dav-2201).

MLA absorption per head: W_q_nope_h (HID,DN) @ W_uk_h^T (DN,DKV) -> w_abs_h (HID,DKV); q_abs = x @ w_abs_h -> (T,HEADS,DKV); scores_nope = einsum('thk,jk->htj', q_abs, c_kv); out = einsum('htj,jk->htk', probs, c_kv) @ W_uv_h. Do NOT reshape W_q_nope to (HEADS*HID,DN) and W_uk to (HEADS*DN,DKV); that mismatches the k-axis.

evidence.source: stg-0009 failure analysis: aclnnMatmul k-axis [4096,64] vs [512,96]

statement: 910B has no SIMT (SWIGLU_HAS_SIMT=0). Tiny rows (half*sizeof(T)<32, large outer) degenerate to 1 element/tile. Fix: load 2*C contiguous elems (DataCopyPad blockCount=1), split even/odd with Gather (c220 has Gather, no DeInterleave), compute, store C contiguous outputs.
invalidators: CANN adds SIMT or DeInterleave for dav_c220

statement: Gather Level 2 on c220: AscendC::Gather(dst, src, srcOffset, 0, count); srcOffset is LocalTensor<uint32_t> [0,2,4,...] / [1,3,...]. Build offsets once per block with SetValue. Use DataCopyPad blockCount=1 for 2*C input and C output; sync V->MTE2 before reusing input.

Gather requires dst and src to have the same element type T. For fp16/bf16 input, Gather into LocalTensor<T> x0/x1 first, then Cast to float; never Gather into a float tensor from a half/bf16 tensor. Offset tensor has one uint32 per output element.

Tiny-row Gather must use distinct buffers: load input into inLocal, Gather even indices into x0Local[T], odd into x1Local[T]. Never Gather in-place or pass the same tensor as x0/x1; the second Gather would read already-overwritten data. 10/12 correctness failure otherwise.

Gather offsets are BYTE offsets, not element indices. chunk(2, dim) splits each row into [first half | second half], not even/odd. For row r and column c: x0=(r*2*half+c)*sizeof(T), x1=(r*2*half+half+c)*sizeof(T).

Verified 910B tiny-row path for SwiGlu: contiguous 2*C load, Gather into separate T buffers with byte offsets, fp32 compute, contiguous C store. 12/12 official cases; 2.96x aggregate; (1000003,2) bf16 0.011x -> 2.58x (8.08ms -> 0.030ms).

AscendC::SwiGLU(dst, src0, src1, beta, count) computes swish(src1)*src0. For silu(x0)*x1 pass src0=x1, src1=x0. Correct on 32B-aligned slices on dav-2201; bf16 is unsupported; keep the manual fp32 chain for bf16/non-aligned/tiny rows.
Verified 910B SwiGlu aligned-path adv API: 12/12, 3.65x aggregate; (1024,2048) fp16 1.88x -> 3.74x. Profile after: VEC 0.703, scalar 0.345, MTE2 0.141, MTE3 0.098; bottleneck VEC.

SwiGlu 910B adv API 3-run median: 3.37x (3.399/3.366/3.343), best 3.65x; baseline run-to-run noise is significant, use median. (1024,2048) fp16 candidate 0.024-0.027ms; aligned adv path, bf16/tiny manual fallback.

910B tiny-row half=1: rowsPerTile=2048 + vector-generated Gather byte offsets (CreateVecIndex/Muls/Adds) reduced kernel duration 28.4->16.4us and scalar ratio 0.874->0.391 (now VEC-bound). rowsPerTile*half must stay on the 128/64 element repeat boundary, or a 4095-element tail gives a UB VEC alignment fault.

910B bf16 has no AscendC::SwiGLU overload. Fuse bf16 SiLU as Cast(bf16->fp32), Silu<float>, Cast(x1->fp32), Mul, Cast(bf16) when n*sizeof(T)%32==0. Result: 12/12; 3-run median 3.55x; bf16 (4096,8192) profile MTE2 0.756/MTE3 0.716, VEC 0.358, scalar 0.117 -> memory-bound.

910B SwiGlu aligned path: vendor-style DataCopy (32B block params) A/B gave 3-run median 3.15x vs 3.55x for DataCopyPad under our tiling; reverted. Profile showed MTE2 0.793/duration 165us but end-to-end was not better; do not retry without changing tile shape/stride.

910B RMSNorm many-row shapes: batch R=min(tile/cols,64) rows per UB tile, one DataCopyPad blockCount=R, whole-tile Cast/Mul, row sums via a zeroed R*64 temp + strided Add + one WholeReduceSum(repeat=R), then per-row Muls/Mul. (65536,64) fp16 0.193x->1.92x, (100000,128) bf16 0.160x->1.28x, 14-case geomean 2.223->3.370, total 0.852->2.802. Requires cols<64 or cols%64==0; partial trailing 64-column groups are not correct yet.

rms_norm3 pitfalls on 910B: (1) calc_row_tiling2 clamps tile to cols, so tile/cols==1 and the batched gate never fires; add calc_row_tiling3 that keeps the multi-row UB budget. (2) Div(rstd, ones, rstd, rh) needs rh ones, not 8, or rows >=8 divide by stale values. (3) A partial trailing 64-column group (cols=80/120) gives wrong sums; gate v3 to cols<64 or cols%64==0 and fall back to v2 otherwise.

910B SwiGlu tiny path was scalar-bound (scalar 0.76-0.92, 55-72us): every kernel launch generated 8192 Gather offsets with scalar SetValue. Vectorize offsets: for step=half (or half/2 when packing 2x16-bit into uint32), off0=(i+(i>>log2(step))*step)*elemBytes when step is a power of two, else q=floor(i/step) via Cast(float)->Muls(1/step)->Adds(0.001)->Cast(CAST_FLOOR); Gather packed uint32 words for even 16-bit half (2x fewer elements). Results: (999983,4) fp16 0.857x->2.29x, (100000,8) bf16 1.078x->2.22x, (50000,16) fp16 1.106x->2.32x, (363,367,14) bf16 0.978x->2.23x; 22-case median geomean 2.384/total 2.605/worst 1.685; candidate ~26us, launch-bound.

910B RMSNorm large-cols: when cols exceed the v2 tile (~6320 for 16-bit, ~4424 for fp32) but one row fits UB, use a 1-deep full-row kernel (qx/qg/qy + row/sq/gamma fp32 + in-place halving ReduceSum) to read x once: (1024,8192) bf16 0.133->0.034ms (1.14x->3.87x), (512,8192) bf16 1.65x->4.66x; memory is cols*(3*es+12). For v3, gamma is row-invariant: one strided Mul per 64 columns with src1RepStride=0 replaces R per-row Mul calls; and size R=min(tile/cols,64) with perElem=3*es+8+red/R+qg/gamma instead of 6*es+16, giving (65536,64) 2.16x and (100000,128) 1.79x. 14-case median geomean 3.846/total 3.600/worst 1.766; (100000,128) remains VEC-bound (VEC 0.86/scalar 0.56/MTE2 0.10).

910B SwiGlu non-aligned rows (half*es>=32 but not a 32B multiple): pad each row to halfA=align_up(half*es,32)/es (511->512) and copy R rows with DataCopyPad(blockCount=R, blockLen=halfA*es, srcStride=(2*half-halfA)*es); run the vector chain on the contiguous padded tile (padding is read but never stored). x0 overread stays inside the row pair; x1's last row needs an exact blockLen=half*es copy. Output stays per-row exact because GM rows are 511 wide. R sized from UB (3 one-deep queues + 2 fp32 scratch); return R=0 and fall back to the main path when one row does not fit. (17,257,1022) fp32 1.51x->2.19x, (4097,1022) fp16 1.51x->2.24x; 22-case median geomean 2.466/total 2.846/worst 2.072; unaligned edge tests 12/12.

evidence.cases: official 12/12, tiny edges 14/14, unaligned edges 12/12, bench 22/22, 3-run median

statement: 910B RMSNorm v3: batching the per-row scalar reads (read rh rstd values into float rv[64], then one S_V for the whole Muls loop) regressed (100000,128) bf16 1.79x->1.29x and (65536,64) fp16 2.16x->1.58x; reverted. Compiler generated worse scalar/stack code. Keep the official per-row GetValue + S_V pattern.

evidence.run: m18 2026-10-28 rms_norm3 batched scalar reads A/B

statement: 910B RMSNorm v3: raising the tile row cap from 64 to 128 halves the tile count for cols=64 and improved (65536,64) fp16 candidate 60.7->56.0us (2.24x->2.50x); (100000,128) barely changes (R 64->65). Memory check: R*cols*(3*es+8) + R*64*4 must stay under 80-90% UB; cols=64 bf16 R=128 uses ~145KB.
